translations.translation: With the help of Heaven*.
Fifteen Tammuz,
the year 5742*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Learning Torah in a group draws a higher revelation of the thirteen attributes of mercy, beyond the measure of the arousal from below.

translations.translation: "Ten who sit and engage in Torah, the Divine Presence dwells among them"1,
and it is explained by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe of the Geulah, in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" that was given for the first celebration of Yud-Beis Tammuz
(the year 5688),
that even one who sits and engages in Torah draws down a revelation of G-dliness,
as the continuation of the Mishnah states: "And from where [do we derive] even five... even three... even two... even one...",
nevertheless,
the drawing down through the Torah of many is a more elevated drawing down.
For just as regarding prayer, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said2
"The prayer of the many is not rejected,"
because through the prayer of the many, the thirteen attributes of mercy that are above the chain of descent are drawn down,
and moreover3
the drawing down from above through the prayer of the many is not commensurate with the measure of their arousal from below
(even not commensurate with the measure of the arousal from below of the many),
so too is it regarding Torah,
that through the study of Torah by the many, there is a drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy that are above the chain of descent
[For although the drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy through the engagement in Torah is due to the virtue of Torah,
that the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded correspond to the thirteen attributes of mercy,
from this it is understood
that the drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy also occurs when one sits and engages in Torah,
nevertheless, the drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy through engagement in Torah is primarily through Torah study specifically in public,
meaning that the level of the thirteen attributes of mercy that is drawn down through engagement in Torah in public is a more elevated level],
and moreover,
the drawing down through the study of Torah by the many is not commensurate with the measure of the study of the many.
B)
And it can be said,
that the analogy of Torah to prayer
is also hinted at in the aforementioned Mishnah: "And from where [do we derive] even one? As it is stated4
'In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you,'"
"In every place" etc. refers to the Holy Temple
[a place where the Divine Presence comes,
"I will come to you"],
where permission was given to pronounce the explicit name
["I cause My name to be mentioned"]5,
and the Holy Temple is related to the pillar of service,
sacrifices6
and prayer7
[And to add,
that even the Priestly Blessing, in which they would mention the Name as it is written in the Holy Temple5,
was after the offering of the daily morning sacrifice8
(the beginning of all the sacrifices),
and also nowadays the Sages instituted the Priestly Blessing in prayer9,
and within the prayer itself – in the blessing of the service10].
And in the Mishnah, this verse is brought
("In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you")
regarding the indwelling of the Divine Presence through the study of Torah,
and from this it is implied that Torah and prayer are related to each other, and specifically in this matter.
